truthAudit.Summary: Truth audit of Run 2 against 20 intentionally visible ground-truth vulnerabilities (SC-V3-001 through SC-V3-020). Run 2 reported 14 findings. 11 of the 20 true vulnerabilities were actually present in Run 2's answer (7 found_full, 4 found_partial). 9 true vulnerabilities were completely missed by Run 2. Run 2 reported 1 additional finding (memory leak) not present in the truth set. Severity corrections apply to 6 findings where Run 2's severity rating diverges from ground truth; these are recorded as corrections and do not affect detection-status flags.

Items.Notes: Run 2 correctly identified the format-string injection in log_debug_message via the runtime log format path, quoting the active_format=runtime_log_format() line and the printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) call. The format_string() variant (snprintf with fmt) was also found in a separate finding. Ground-truth anchors (log_format; runtime_log_format; printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input)) are all present in the quote.

Run 2 identified the fact() function and the integer overflow risk (CWE-190) but did not quote the actual overflowing loop body (result *= i). The ground-truth anchor 'result *= i' is the precise overflow site at lines 316-318 and was not quoted. The finding is correct in substance but partial in evidence.

Run 2 quoted both the scratch allocation/enqueue in stage_deferred_history_flush and the cleanup() calls including memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup(). However, the critical TOCTOU-style UAF link — that cleanup() is called IMMEDIATELY after stage_deferred_history_flush() within the same cleanup() function (lines 883-884 in source), freeing pool memory while the 25ms-delayed worker still references scratch — is only implied in the impact text, not explicit in the quoted evidence. The ground-truth anchor sequence (stage_deferred_history_flush; memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup; sleep_for; scratch) spans two functions whose adjacency in cleanup() is the actual trigger.

Run 2 did not report command injection via validate_config(). The source shows validator_cmd + ' ' + config_file passed to system(command.c_str()) at lines 563-569, with both values attacker-controllable via config settings loaded through the path-traversal vulnerability. Run 2's command-injection finding only covered execute_admin_command's 'exec' subcommand, not validate_config's 'validate' subcommand.

Run 2 correctly identified the stack buffer overflow in evaluate_expression, quoting the strcpy branch triggered when expression.length() >= sizeof(input_buffer_). Ground-truth anchors (strcpy(input_buffer_; dest[src_len]; src_len > dest_size) are satisfied: the strcpy without bounds checking and the 1024-byte input_buffer_ are both present. The safe_string_copy off-by-one was reported as a separate finding and is evaluated against SC-V3-005's anchors (stack buffer, evaluate_expression) — this finding matches SC-V3-005 fully.

Run 2 correctly identified the data race in ThreadSafeCounter::increment, quoting the read of value_ outside the lock_guard and the stale old_value assignment. Ground-truth anchors (volatile long long; old_value = value_; lock_guard; value_ = old_value + 1) are all present in the quote.

Run 2 correctly identified the logic bomb / emergency override backdoor in AdminConsole::authenticate, quoting login_attempts_ > 5, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE, and authenticated_ = true. Ground-truth anchors (login_attempts_ > 5; EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE; authenticated_ = true) are all present in the quote.

Run 2 correctly identified path traversal in load_config, quoting config_dir_ + filename and the lack of path validation. Ground-truth anchors (config_dir_ + filename; load_config(filename)) are present. Note: this finding also exhibits the TOCTOU pattern (sleep_for between exists and open), but Run 2 assessed it only as path traversal, which matches the ground-truth CWE-22 classification.

Items.Notes: Run 2 identified the heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse with the 256-byte buffer and unbounded strcpy. However, the ground-truth anchor points to schedule_expression_analysis as the entry point (the scheduled task that invokes parse), and Run 2's finding isolates parse() without connecting it to the scheduled-analysis path. The buffer_size_ = 256 and strcpy anchors are present, making this a partial match.

Run 2 correctly identified the hardcoded administrator credentials, quoting the exact ADMIN_SECRET and SC_ENT_2025_AUTH values. Ground-truth anchors (ADMIN_SECRET; SC_ENT_2025_AUTH) are present in the quote.

Run 2 did not report the weak PRNG for session tokens. The source shows generate_session_token() using std::mt19937 seeded by std::random_device with std::uniform_int_distribution<>(1000, 9999), producing only 4-digit tokens that are trivially brute-forced. None of Run 2's 14 findings mention session token generation, mt19937, or uniform_int_distribution.

Run 2 did not report the thread-unsafe timestamp cache. The source shows a static std::tm cached_time with localtime (non-reentrant) and cached_time = *local_time at lines 230-231 inside log_debug_message, which is a data race under concurrent logging. None of Run 2's findings mention cached_time, localtime, or the timestamp cache.

Run 2 did not report insecure temporary file handling. The source's append_override_audit_event() reads TEMP/TMPDIR environment variables and writes supercalc_emergency.log via system() at lines 622-633. None of Run 2's findings mention TEMP, TMPDIR, or the emergency log file.

Run 2 did not report persistent authentication state. The source retains authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ on the AdminConsole instance after authentication without any logout/clear mechanism. None of Run 2's findings mention the persistence of these fields across sessions.

Run 2 did not report the unhandled exception in variable parsing. The source calls std::stod(tokens[3]) at line 729 inside handle_variable_command, which can throw std::invalid_argument or std::out_of_range for non-numeric input. While the surrounding evaluate_expression has a catch block, handle_variable_command's stod call is not within that try block. None of Run 2's findings mention std::stod in handle_variable_command.

Run 2 did not report the integer underflow in memory-pool block split. The source computes remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES at line 133, where SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES is 64 (line 132). If previous_size is smaller than size + 64, the subtraction underflows, producing a huge remaining value. None of Run 2's findings mention SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES, the remaining calculation, or block-split underflow.

Run 2 did not report unbounded recursion in the parser. The source's parse_expression -> parse_term -> parse_factor chain recursively calls parse_expression on PAREN_OPEN at line 428 without any depth check, enabling stack exhaustion on deeply nested parentheses. MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH (256) is defined in config but never used in the parser. None of Run 2's findings mention recursive parsing or recursion depth.

Run 2 did not report the data race in the result cache. The source's evaluate_cached accesses result_cache_ at lines 446-451 without acquiring cache_mutex_ (which is declared but only used elsewhere), while thread_pool_->enqueue at line 808 calls evaluate_cached concurrently. None of Run 2's findings mention result_cache_ or cache_mutex_.

Run 2 did not report the TOCTOU in config loading. The source checks std::filesystem::exists at line 544, then sleeps_for 25ms at line 545, then opens std::ifstream at line 546 — a classic time-of-check-to-time-of-use window. Run 2's path-traversal finding quoted these same lines but assessed only path traversal, not the TOCTOU race. The ground-truth CWE-367 anchor (std::filesystem::exists; sleep_for; std::ifstream file) was not identified as a TOCTOU.

Run 2 did not report integer division by zero in command routing. The source's calculate_route_score computes 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) at line 752, where token_length can be 0 if the input is empty or only whitespace, causing division by zero. None of Run 2's findings mention calculate_route_score or token_length.
